differential_expression_by_gene_disease.name: differential_expression_by_gene_disease
differential_expression_by_gene_disease.body_sql:
SELECT
  gene_symbol,
  doid,
  log2fc,
  pvalue,
  adjpvalue,
  statistical_significance,
  expression_change_direction,
  subjects_up,
  subjects_down,
  subjects_nochange,
  subjects_nocoverage,
  subjects_total
FROM differential_expression

params.description: Per-gene × per-disease differential expression summary (log2 fold change, p-values, significance and per-subject direction counts).
params.when_to_use: Report the differential expression result for a specific gene and disease (DOID). | Rank or filter genes for a disease by effect size (log2fc), significance (adjpvalue/pvalue) or direction. | Join as a fact-level source of gene×disease differential-expression metrics when computing downstream aggregates (e.g., counts of significant biomarkers per disease). | Compose with gene- or disease-level dimension tables (annotations, names) to present human-readable labels without changing measures. | Exclude from direct join to raw subject-level tables or other one-to-many result sets unless re-aggregated, to avoid double-counting subject counts.
params.output_schema: gene_symbol: gene symbol identifying the gene tested — directly from differential_expression.gene_symbol | doid: disease ontology id for the disease tested — directly from differential_expression.doid | log2fc: log2 fold change of expression between comparison groups for this gene×disease — directly from differential_expression.log2fc | pvalue: nominal p-value for the differential expression test — directly from differential_expression.pvalue | adjpvalue: multiple-test-adjusted p-value (e.g., FDR) for the test — directly from differential_expression.adjpvalue | statistical_significance: boolean or categorical flag indicating whether the test passed a significance cutoff (as stored) — directly from differential_expression.statistical_significance | expression_change_direction: categorical direction of change ('up','down','no_change', etc.) as stored — directly from differential_expression.expression_change_direction | subjects_up: integer count of subjects/samples showing up-regulation for this gene in the comparison — directly from differential_expression.subjects_up | subjects_down: integer count of subjects/samples showing down-regulation — directly from differential_expression.subjects_down | subjects_nochange: integer count of subjects/samples with no change called — directly from differential_expression.subjects_nochange | subjects_nocoverage: integer count of subjects/samples without coverage for this gene — directly from differential_expression.subjects_nocoverage | subjects_total: integer total number of subjects/samples considered for this gene×disease test — directly from differential_expression.subjects_total
params.grounded_columns: differential_expression.gene_symbol | differential_expression.doid | differential_expression.log2fc | differential_expression.pvalue | differential_expression.adjpvalue | differential_expression.statistical_significance | differential_expression.expression_change_direction | differential_expression.subjects_up | differential_expression.subjects_down | differential_expression.subjects_nochange | differential_expression.subjects_nocoverage | differential_expression.subjects_total
params.metric: log2fc = differential_expression.log2fc | pvalue = differential_expression.pvalue | adjpvalue = differential_expression.adjpvalue | statistical_significance = differential_expression.statistical_significance | expression_change_direction = differential_expression.expression_change_direction | subjects_up = differential_expression.subjects_up | subjects_down = differential_expression.subjects_down | subjects_nochange = differential_expression.subjects_nochange | subjects_nocoverage = differential_expression.subjects_nocoverage | subjects_total = differential_expression.subjects_total
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to gene_ensembl_to_uniprot_map (JOIN) on gene_symbol (or mapped gene id) — safe because gene_ensembl_to_uniprot_map is a gene-level mapping; it is expected to be one-row-per-gene (or can be de-duplicated) so this view's per-gene×disease measures will not be multiplied. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to disease_summary (NORM) on doid — safe because disease_summary is a disease-level one-row-per-doid summary; joining preserves one row per gene×disease in this view. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to anatomical_entity_lookup (NORM) only if you first have a one-row-per-anatomy key on the view; do not assume anatomy joins are safe unless you join on a single anatomy id per row. | do NOT join without re-aggregation to biomarker_with_aliases_and_articles (JOIN) or biomarker_fda_tests_w_drugs_ncit (JOIN) or biomarker_edrn_with_anatomy (JOIN) if those sibling views are one-to-many (e.g., multiple aliases, articles, drugs, tests per gene or biomarker) because that will duplicate this view's subject counts and other measures. If you must join, aggregate the many-side (e.g., array_agg of distinct attributes or counts) back to one row per gene (or gene×doid) before combining with this view. | do NOT join directly to disease_mutation_with_annotations (JOIN) or fda_test_rank_by_gene_count (RANK) if they are one-to-many per gene or per disease without first summarizing (e.g., count distinct mutations per gene×doid) because such joins will multiply measures like subjects_total; instead, pre-aggregate mutation/test details to one-row-per-gene×doid keyed by gene_symbol and doid and then join. | When composing higher-level aggregates (for example: number of significant genes per disease), use this view as the atomic fact table and aggregate columns such as COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE statistical_significance) or SUM(CASE WHEN expression_change_direction='up' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) — do not sum subjects_* across joined duplicate rows produced by unguarded joins. | If you need to join by gene_symbol to other gene-level sources that legitimately have multiple rows per gene (e.g., multiple Ensembl IDs, multiple aliases), first reduce those sources to one row per gene_symbol (for example choose canonical id or aggregate attributes) to maintain cardinality safety.

differential_expression_by_gene_disease.description: Normalized/deduplicated differential expression measurements at the gene_symbol + doid grain with preserved statistical and subject-count fields. Useful as a cleaned projection for downstream joins, filtering by significance, or aggregations by gene or disease. | Use for: Which genes are differentially expressed for a disease (by doid)?; Filter differential expression results by significance or fold-change and join to gene/biomarker tables; Aggregate number of significant genes per disease or compare subject counts across diseases
counter_examples: Show the pvalue of differential expression of lung cancer

healthy_expression_by_gene_anatomy.name: healthy_expression_by_gene_anatomy
healthy_expression_by_gene_anatomy.body_sql:
SELECT
  ensembl_gene_id,
  uberon_anatomical_id,
  uberon_developmental_id,
  expression_level_gene_relative,
  expression_level_anatomical_relative,
  call_quality,
  expression_rank_score,
  expression_score
FROM healthy_expression

params.description: Provides per-gene × per-anatomy (and anatomy developmental stage) healthy tissue expression measurements and quality/score annotations.
params.when_to_use: Find which anatomical structures (and developmental stages) a given Ensembl gene is expressed in healthy samples and how strongly, relative to that gene and relative to that anatomy. | Rank or filter genes by expression within an anatomical structure or by anatomy-relative expression. | Compose with gene, anatomy, or disease views when you need a stable one-row-per(gene,anatomy,development) expression record to join against (e.g., to attach gene metadata, anatomy labels, or disease associations) without changing expression measures. | Build aggregated summaries (e.g., count of genes expressed in an anatomy) by aggregating the view’s rows rather than by joining a one-to-many detail table.
params.output_schema: ensembl_gene_id: Ensembl gene identifier (directly from healthy_expression.ensembl_gene_id) | uberon_anatomical_id: UBERON anatomical entity identifier for the tissue/structure (directly from healthy_expression.uberon_anatomical_id) | uberon_developmental_id: UBERON developmental stage identifier associated with the anatomy/tissue (directly from healthy_expression.uberon_developmental_id) | expression_level_gene_relative: qualitative or categorical expression level of this gene in this anatomy, expressed relative to other tissues for the same gene (from healthy_expression.expression_level_gene_relative) | expression_level_anatomical_relative: qualitative or categorical expression level of this gene relative to other genes in the same anatomy (from healthy_expression.expression_level_anatomical_relative) | call_quality: quality/status annotation of the call (e.g., high/low/uncertain) (from healthy_expression.call_quality) | expression_rank_score: numeric rank-based score used for ordering expression for this gene×anatomy (from healthy_expression.expression_rank_score) | expression_score: numeric expression magnitude score (e.g., normalized expression) (from healthy_expression.expression_score)
params.metric: expression_level_gene_relative = raw categorical column healthy_expression.expression_level_gene_relative (no aggregation in view) | expression_level_anatomical_relative = raw categorical column healthy_expression.expression_level_anatomical_relative (no aggregation in view) | call_quality = raw categorical/quality column healthy_expression.call_quality (no aggregation in view) | expression_rank_score = numeric column healthy_expression.expression_rank_score (treated as a measure that ranks gene×anatomy pairs; the view does not re-aggregate it) | expression_score = numeric column healthy_expression.expression_score (numeric measure representing expression magnitude; the view surfaces the base value from healthy_expression)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to gene_ensembl_to_uniprot_map on ensembl_gene_id — safe because gene_ensembl_to_uniprot_map is expected to be one-row-per-ensembl_gene_id (or can be normalized to that) so joining will attach gene identifiers/annotations without duplicating expression measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to anatomical_entity_lookup on uberon_anatomical_id — safe because anatomical_entity_lookup is a dimension table keyed by uberon_anatomical_id (one-row per anatomical id) and will not multiply rows or change expression measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to disease_summary or differential_expression_by_gene_disease only when joining on ensembl_gene_id and using those views' aggregated measures (ensure the target is one-row-per-gene or that you aggregate the target to one row per gene first) — safe if the other view is one-row-per-gene; otherwise re-aggregate before joining to avoid duplication. | do NOT join without re-aggregation to biomarker_with_aliases_and_articles, biomarker_fda_tests_w_drugs_ncit, biomarker_edrn_with_anatomy, or disease_mutation_with_annotations if those sibling views are one-to-many (e.g., a gene with many articles, drugs, mutations or biomarkers). Joining directly will multiply this view's rows and therefore multiply expression_score/expression_rank_score unless you first aggregate the many-side to one row per join key (e.g., count, max, or other summary). | do NOT join directly to fda_test_rank_by_gene_count (RANK) if it is a many-row ranking per gene; instead ensure the rank view is one-row-per-gene or aggregate it to that grain before joining. If you need to enrich expression rows with multiple related records (e.g., many articles per gene), attach them via a separate query or use lateral/array aggregation so the expression measures remain one-per(gene,anatomy,development). | When composing further measures (SUM, AVG) over expression_score or expression_rank_score, aggregate over the view's grain (ensembl_gene_id, uberon_anatomical_id, uberon_developmental_id) to preserve correctness; do not rely on implicit de-duplication via joins to many-side tables.

healthy_expression_by_gene_anatomy.description: Projection of healthy tissue expression calls at the ensembl_gene_id + uberon_anatomical_id + uberon_developmental_id grain including expression scores and ranks. Useful for tissue-specific expression lookups and joins to anatomical entities or gene mappings. | Use for: What tissues show high expression for a given gene (by ensembl_gene_id)?; Compare expression ranks/scores across anatomical terms or developmental stages; Join to anatomical_entity to show tissue names for expression records

biomarker_with_aliases_and_articles.name: biomarker_with_aliases_and_articles
biomarker_with_aliases_and_articles.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id,
  b.gene_symbol,
  b.biomarker_description,
  b.biomarker_id,
  b.test_is_a_panel,
  ba.alias,
  ba.biomarker_internal_id AS biomarker_internal_id,
  ba.alias AS alias_from_ba,
  ba.alias AS alias_duplicate_holder,
  bm.pmid
FROM biomarker b
LEFT JOIN biomarker_alias ba
  ON ba.biomarker_internal_id = b.id
LEFT JOIN biomarker_article bm
  ON bm.biomarker_internal_id = b.id

params.description: Provides biomarker rows with their aliases and linked article PMIDs — answers which aliases and literature (pmid) are associated with each biomarker.
params.when_to_use: List aliases for a given biomarker id, gene symbol, or internal id | Find literature (pmid) references associated with biomarkers | Compose with other gene/disease/anatomy views when you need biomarker-level rows enriched with alias text and article pmids | Filter biomarkers by alias text or by presence/absence of pmid before aggregating or joining to other dimensions
params.output_schema: id: biomarker.id — primary internal identifier for the biomarker (source: biomarker.id) | gene_symbol: biomarker.gene_symbol — gene symbol associated with the biomarker (source: biomarker.gene_symbol) | biomarker_description: biomarker.biomarker_description — human-readable description of the biomarker (source: biomarker.biomarker_description) | biomarker_id: biomarker.biomarker_id — external or canonical biomarker identifier (source: biomarker.biomarker_id) | test_is_a_panel: biomarker.test_is_a_panel — boolean/flag indicating if the test is a panel (source: biomarker.test_is_a_panel) | alias: biomarker_alias.alias — alias text coming from biomarker_alias table (source: biomarker_alias.alias) | biomarker_internal_id: biomarker_alias.biomarker_internal_id AS biomarker_internal_id — foreign key in biomarker_alias pointing to biomarker.id (source: biomarker_alias.biomarker_internal_id) | alias_from_ba: biomarker_alias.alias AS alias_from_ba — same alias reproduced from biomarker_alias (source: biomarker_alias.alias) | alias_duplicate_holder: biomarker_alias.alias AS alias_duplicate_holder — duplicate of alias column (source: biomarker_alias.alias) | pmid: biomarker_article.pmid — PubMed ID(s) linked to the biomarker from biomarker_article (source: biomarker_article.pmid)
params.grounded_columns: biomarker.id | biomarker.gene_symbol | biomarker.biomarker_description | biomarker.biomarker_id | biomarker.test_is_a_panel | biomarker_alias.alias | biomarker_alias.biomarker_internal_id | biomarker_article.pmid
params.metric: No aggregated metrics are defined in this view; all output columns are direct base columns or direct copies. Example derived expressions present in SQL: biomarker_internal_id = biomarker_alias.biomarker_internal_id (passthrough). There are no SUM/COUNT/AVG aggregates in this view.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension tables that are one-row-per-biomarker on biomarker.id (or biomarker_internal_id) without re-aggregation — safe examples: join to disease_summary on biomarker.id if disease_summary is one-row-per-biomarker (join key: biomarker.id = disease_summary.biomarker_id) — safe because this view is many-rows-per-biomarker only due to aliases or pmids but the join to a one-row-per-biomarker dimension will not multiply those dimension rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to gene_ensembl_to_uniprot_map on gene symbol or gene id when that mapping is one-to-one — safe when the target map is one-row-per-gene (join key: biomarker.gene_symbol = gene_ensembl_to_uniprot_map.gene_symbol). | do NOT naïvely join to one-to-many tables/views (e.g., biomarker_alias, biomarker_article, disease_mutation_with_annotations, biomarker_edrn_with_anatomy) without handling multiplicity because this view already includes LEFT JOINs to biomarker_alias and biomarker_article and therefore can contain multiple rows per biomarker due to aliases and pmids. Joining another one-to-many table will multiply rows and duplicate any measures/rows. | If you need to compose this view with other one-to-many relationships, either: (a) pre-aggregate the one-to-many side to one-row-per-biomarker (for example, group biomarker_article by biomarker_internal_id and collect pmid or count pmids) before joining, or (b) aggregate this view to the desired grain (e.g., one-row-per-biomarker) first by applying GROUP BY biomarker.id and appropriate aggregations (e.g., array_agg(alias) or count(pmid)). | Specific safe joins in this database context: safe to join to anatomical_entity_lookup or disease_summary only if those are known to be one-row-per-key dimensions keyed by an identifier that maps 1:1 to biomarker (use the biomarker.id or biomarker.gene_symbol mapping as appropriate) — verify the target view/table grain before joining. | Summary rule for planners: treat this view as grain = ['id','alias','pmid'] (as declared). Any join on biomarker.id to a table that is one-row-per-biomarker will not duplicate measures. Any join to tables with multiple rows per biomarker must be preceded by aggregation on that side or you must aggregate this view to a coarser grain first.

biomarker_with_aliases_and_articles.description: Denormalized biomarker-level relation joining biomarker core attributes with all aliases and linked article PMIDs. One row per biomarker alias + article combination (multiplicative). Useful for text/display, filtering by alias or PMID, or aggregating counts of aliases/articles per biomarker. | Use for: List biomarkers with their aliases and supporting literature; Count number of aliases or articles per biomarker; Filter biomarkers by alias text or PMID and join back to biomarker attributes

biomarker_fda_tests_w_drugs_ncit.name: biomarker_fda_tests_w_drugs_ncit
biomarker_fda_tests_w_drugs_ncit.body_sql:
SELECT
  bf.id,
  bf.test_trade_name,
  bf.test_submission,
  bft.test_manufacturer,
  bft.biomarker_origin,
  bft.doid,
  bft.histological_type,
  bft.specimen_type,
  bft.platform_method,
  bft.test_number_genes,
  bft.test_adoption_evidence,
  bft.test_approval_status,
  bft.test_study_design,
  bft.clinical_significance,
  bfdd.biomarker_drug,
  bfn.ncit_biomarker
FROM biomarker_fda bf
LEFT JOIN biomarker_fda_test bft
  ON bft.test_trade_name = bf.test_trade_name
  AND bft.test_submission = bf.test_submission
LEFT JOIN biomarker_fda_drug bfdd
  ON bfdd.biomarker_fda_id = bf.id
LEFT JOIN biomarker_fda_ncit_term bfn
  ON bfn.biomarker_fda_id = bf.id

params.description: Provides FDA biomarker test records enriched with linked drugs and NCIt biomarker terms to support queries about tests, their properties, associated drugs, and ontology mappings.
params.when_to_use: List FDA biomarker tests with detailed test properties and their associated drugs and NCIt terms | Filter or group tests by manufacturer, biomarker origin, specimen type, platform/method, approval status, or clinical significance | Join test-level information to drug or ontology-focused views when building compound queries about tests and targeted therapies | As a base for counts/aggregates of tests (e.g., number of tests per manufacturer or number of drugs linked to a test) when careful about cardinality
params.output_schema: id: unique identifier for the FDA biomarker record (derived from biomarker_fda.id) | test_trade_name: trade name of the test (derived from biomarker_fda.test_trade_name) | test_submission: submission identifier/date for the test (derived from biomarker_fda.test_submission) | test_manufacturer: manufacturer of the test (derived from biomarker_fda_test.test_manufacturer) | biomarker_origin: origin/source of the biomarker used in the test (derived from biomarker_fda_test.biomarker_origin) | doid: Disease Ontology ID associated with the test (derived from biomarker_fda_test.doid) | histological_type: histological type annotation for the test (derived from biomarker_fda_test.histological_type) | specimen_type: specimen type required/used by the test (derived from biomarker_fda_test.specimen_type) | platform_method: assay platform or method used by the test (derived from biomarker_fda_test.platform_method) | test_number_genes: number of genes included in the test panel (derived from biomarker_fda_test.test_number_genes) | test_adoption_evidence: evidence of adoption for the test (derived from biomarker_fda_test.test_adoption_evidence) | test_approval_status: FDA approval status of the test (derived from biomarker_fda_test.test_approval_status) | test_study_design: study design information for the test submission (derived from biomarker_fda_test.test_study_design) | clinical_significance: clinical significance annotation for the test (derived from biomarker_fda_test.clinical_significance) | biomarker_drug: drug associated with the biomarker FDA record (derived from biomarker_fda_drug.biomarker_drug) | ncit_biomarker: NCIt ontology term mapped to the biomarker FDA record (derived from biomarker_fda_ncit_term.ncit_biomarker)
params.grounded_columns: biomarker_fda.id | biomarker_fda.test_trade_name | biomarker_fda.test_submission | biomarker_fda_test.test_manufacturer | biomarker_fda_test.biomarker_origin | biomarker_fda_test.doid | biomarker_fda_test.histological_type | biomarker_fda_test.specimen_type | biomarker_fda_test.platform_method | biomarker_fda_test.test_number_genes | biomarker_fda_test.test_adoption_evidence | biomarker_fda_test.test_approval_status | biomarker_fda_test.test_study_design | biomarker_fda_test.clinical_significance | biomarker_fda_drug.biomarker_drug | biomarker_fda_drug.biomarker_fda_id | biomarker_fda_ncit_term.ncit_biomarker | biomarker_fda_ncit_term.biomarker_fda_id
params.metric: row_is_observation = 1  -- this view is at the grain of biomarker_fda.id x biomarker_drug x ncit_biomarker as produced by LEFT JOINs; no aggregated measures are computed here | test_gene_count = biomarker_fda_test.test_number_genes  -- passthrough numeric metric representing panel gene count when present
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimensional lookups that are one-row-per-key on their key columns without duplicating measures, for example: |   - Join to biomarker_with_aliases_and_articles on id = id (safe) — this view has one row per biomarker_fda.id × biomarker_drug × ncit_biomarker; joining by biomarker_fda.id to a view guaranteed to be one-row-per-id will not multiply test-level rows beyond the existing drug/NCIt multiplicity. |   - Join to disease_summary on disease_summary.doid = biomarker_fda_test.doid (safe) — disease_summary is a disease-level normalization (one-row-per-doid), so joining preserves this view's row multiplicity. | Do NOT join without re-aggregation to views/tables that are one-to-many from the same key space because they will multiply this view's rows/measures: |   - Do NOT join directly to biomarker_fda_drug (or any table that lists multiple drugs per biomarker_fda_id) on biomarker_fda.id without aggregating drugs first, because biomarker_fda_drug is one-to-many and would duplicate rows for each drug; this view already LEFT JOINed biomarker_fda_drug producing biomarker_drug values and may already expose multiple rows per id. |   - Do NOT join to biomarker_fda_ncit_term (or similar one-to-many ontology mapping tables) on biomarker_fda.id without aggregation, because those mappings are one-to-many and will multiply rows; this view already includes ncit_biomarker values via LEFT JOIN. | If you need aggregated measures (e.g., count of distinct drugs per biomarker_fda.id or number of NCIt terms linked), compute them from the base tables with GROUP BY biomarker_fda.id or aggregate this view first using GROUP BY id to avoid overcounting caused by join duplication. | When composing with other JOIN views (e.g., differential_expression_by_gene_disease, gene_ensembl_to_uniprot_map), join on stable keys that are one-to-one or many-to-one into those views (for example, join by doid to disease-normalized views or by gene identifiers only if the other view is one-row-per-gene), and if the other side is one-to-many, perform aggregation on that side before joining.

biomarker_fda_tests_w_drugs_ncit.description: Denormalized view of FDA biomarker/test metadata joining biomarker_fda, biomarker_fda_test, related drugs, and NCIt terms. One row per test_trade_name + test_submission + drug + ncit term combination (multiplicative). Useful for exploring test attributes alongside drugs and ontology terms or aggregating drug lists per test. | Use for: Which FDA tests target a given disease (doid) or histological type?; List drugs associated with an FDA biomarker/test and related ontology terms; Aggregate tests by approval status or manufacturer

disease_mutation_with_annotations.name: disease_mutation_with_annotations
disease_mutation_with_annotations.body_sql:
SELECT
  dm.id,
  dm.chromosome_id,
  dm.chromosome_pos,
  dm.ref_nt,
  dm.alt_nt,
  dm.ensembl_transcript_id,
  dm.cds_pos,
  dm.peptide_pos,
  dm.aa_pos_uniprotkb,
  dm.ref_aa,
  dm.alt_aa,
  dm.mutation_freq,
  dm.data_source,
  dm.doid,
  dma.pmid,
  dmip.site_prediction,
  dmip.probability,
  dmip.tool,
  dmsa.description AS site_description,
  dmsa.feature_key,
  dmt.uberon_anatomical_id
FROM disease_mutation dm
LEFT JOIN disease_mutation_article dma
  ON dma.disease_mutation_id = dm.id
LEFT JOIN disease_mutation_impact_prediction dmip
  ON dmip.disease_mutation_id = dm.id
LEFT JOIN disease_mutation_site_annotation dmsa
  ON dmsa.disease_mutation_id = dm.id
LEFT JOIN disease_mutation_tissue dmt
  ON dmt.disease_mutation_id = dm.id

params.description: Row-level disease-associated mutation annotations combining core mutation attributes with article links, impact predictions, site annotations, and tissue (anatomy) mappings.
params.when_to_use: List or filter individual disease-associated mutations and their molecular/protein coordinates and annotations | Retrieve supporting articles (pmid) and predicted impact (site_prediction, probability, tool) for specific mutations | Join mutation-level data to anatomical context (uberon_anatomical_id) for downstream aggregation by tissue/anatomy | Compose gene- or disease-level summaries by aggregating this mutation-level view (e.g., mutation counts, average probability) after re-aggregation
params.output_schema: id: Unique identifier for the disease_mutation row — derived from disease_mutation.id | chromosome_id: Chromosome identifier (e.g., '1','X') — derived from disease_mutation.chromosome_id | chromosome_pos: Genomic position on the chromosome — derived from disease_mutation.chromosome_pos | ref_nt: Reference nucleotide at the mutation site — derived from disease_mutation.ref_nt | alt_nt: Alternate nucleotide at the mutation site — derived from disease_mutation.alt_nt | ensembl_transcript_id: Ensembl transcript identifier the mutation maps to — derived from disease_mutation.ensembl_transcript_id | cds_pos: Position in the coding sequence (CDS) — derived from disease_mutation.cds_pos | peptide_pos: Position in the peptide sequence — derived from disease_mutation.peptide_pos | aa_pos_uniprotkb: Amino-acid position according to UniProtKB numbering — derived from disease_mutation.aa_pos_uniprotkb | ref_aa: Reference amino acid — derived from disease_mutation.ref_aa | alt_aa: Alternate amino acid — derived from disease_mutation.alt_aa | mutation_freq: Observed mutation frequency (as stored) — derived from disease_mutation.mutation_freq | data_source: Source system or dataset for the mutation record — derived from disease_mutation.data_source | doid: Disease Ontology ID associated with the mutation — derived from disease_mutation.doid | pmid: PubMed ID linking an article to this mutation — derived from disease_mutation_article.pmid (may be NULL due to LEFT JOIN) | site_prediction: Predicted impact label for the mutation site (e.g., deleterious) — derived from disease_mutation_impact_prediction.site_prediction (may be NULL) | probability: Numeric confidence/probability associated with the site_prediction — derived from disease_mutation_impact_prediction.probability (may be NULL) | tool: Name of the prediction tool that produced the site_prediction/probability — derived from disease_mutation_impact_prediction.tool (may be NULL) | site_description: Free-text description of the annotated site (e.g., domain, motif) — derived from disease_mutation_site_annotation.description (aliased as site_description; may be NULL) | feature_key: Key/type of the site feature (e.g., 'domain','motif') — derived from disease_mutation_site_annotation.feature_key (may be NULL) | uberon_anatomical_id: Uberon anatomy identifier mapping the mutation to tissue/anatomical context — derived from disease_mutation_tissue.uberon_anatomical_id (may be NULL)
params.grounded_columns: disease_mutation.id | disease_mutation.chromosome_id | disease_mutation.chromosome_pos | disease_mutation.ref_nt | disease_mutation.alt_nt | disease_mutation.ensembl_transcript_id | disease_mutation.cds_pos | disease_mutation.peptide_pos | disease_mutation.aa_pos_uniprotkb | disease_mutation.ref_aa | disease_mutation.alt_aa | disease_mutation.mutation_freq | disease_mutation.data_source | disease_mutation.doid | disease_mutation_article.pmid | disease_mutation_impact_prediction.site_prediction | disease_mutation_impact_prediction.probability | disease_mutation_impact_prediction.tool | disease_mutation_site_annotation.description | disease_mutation_site_annotation.feature_key | disease_mutation_tissue.uberon_anatomical_id
params.metric: mutation_count = COUNT(1) over an aggregation of this view by desired grouping (e.g., by doid or uberon_anatomical_id). This view itself is at the mutation-row grain; no precomputed aggregate metrics are included. | avg_prediction_probability = AVG(probability) over grouped rows where probability IS NOT NULL (must aggregate this view) | distinct_pmid_count = COUNT(DISTINCT pmid) over grouped rows (LEFT JOINed pmid can be NULL; count distinct handles duplicates) | note: all 'metrics' are derived via standard SQL aggregations on the rows of this view; there are no in-view aggregate expressions.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to disease_summary on disease_mutation.doid = disease_summary.doid — safe because disease_summary is a disease-level (one-row-per-doid) normalized view; joining will not duplicate mutation rows and preserves row-level measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to anatomical_entity_lookup on disease_mutation_tissue.uberon_anatomical_id = anatomical_entity_lookup.uberon_id — safe because anatomical_entity_lookup is one-row-per-uberon_id (normal lookup); it enriches anatomy metadata without duplicating mutation rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to gene_ensembl_to_uniprot_map on disease_mutation.ensembl_transcript_id = gene_ensembl_to_uniprot_map.ensembl_transcript_id — safe if gene_ensembl_to_uniprot_map is one-row-per-transcript mapping; verify it is unique on ensembl_transcript_id to avoid multiplying rows. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views such as disease_mutation_article, disease_mutation_impact_prediction, disease_mutation_site_annotation, or disease_mutation_tissue without re-aggregation — the current view already LEFT JOINs those tables and may produce multiple rows per disease_mutation.id when there are multiple related rows. Joining another one-to-many dataset on disease_mutation.id would further multiply rows and inflate counts/averages unless you first aggregate the one-to-many data (e.g., per mutation: COUNT(DISTINCT pmid), MAX(probability), ARRAY_AGG(DISTINCT feature_key)) and then join on id. | When composing higher-level aggregations (e.g., mutation_count per disease or anatomy), always aggregate this view at the desired grouping level rather than relying on row counts after joining additional many-to-many dimensions. | If you need to attach multiple related items (e.g., multiple pmids or multiple site annotations) without collapsing to single rows, join this view to those detail tables and then distinct-aggregate or use ARRAY_AGG/DISTINCT to avoid accidental duplication of measures.

disease_mutation_with_annotations.description: Mutation-centric view joining disease_mutation with related articles, impact predictions, site annotations, and tissue mappings. One row per disease_mutation plus any related annotation/prediction/article/tissue (multiplicative). Useful for surfacing mutation context, evidence pmids, predicted impacts, and tissue associations. | Use for: What annotations and evidence exist for a given mutation id?; Find mutations occurring in a given tissue (uberon id) or associated with high-impact predictions; Aggregate number of articles or predictions per mutation
validated_on: Show all information about disease mutations

gene_ensembl_to_uniprot_map.name: gene_ensembl_to_uniprot_map
gene_ensembl_to_uniprot_map.body_sql:
SELECT
  x.gene_symbol,
  x.ensembl_gene_id,
  x.speciesid,
  mpd.uniprotkb_ac,
  muc.uniprotkb_canonical_ac
FROM xref_gene_ensembl x
LEFT JOIN map_protein_disease_mutation mpd
  ON mpd.ensembl_transcript_id = x.ensembl_gene_id
LEFT JOIN map_uniprot_canonical_id muc
  ON muc.uniprotkb_ac = mpd.uniprotkb_ac

params.description: Maps Ensembl gene identifiers to UniProt accessions (including canonical accession) and provides the gene symbol and species id for each mapping.
params.when_to_use: Find UniProt accession(s) (including canonical accession) associated with a given Ensembl gene id | Resolve Ensembl-to-UniProt mapping when annotating gene-level results with protein accessions | Compose gene-level result sets with UniProt identifiers for downstream joins to protein-centric resources | Filter or group differential/healthy expression results by UniProt accession after joining by Ensembl gene id
params.output_schema: gene_symbol: gene name/symbol coming from table xref_gene_ensembl.gene_symbol | ensembl_gene_id: Ensembl gene identifier coming from table xref_gene_ensembl.ensembl_gene_id (this view's grain includes this column) | speciesid: species identifier coming from table xref_gene_ensembl.speciesid | uniprotkb_ac: UniProt accession coming from table map_protein_disease_mutation.uniprotkb_ac (may be NULL when no mapping exists) | uniprotkb_canonical_ac: UniProt canonical accession coming from table map_uniprot_canonical_id.uniprotkb_canonical_ac (may be NULL when no canonical mapping exists)
params.metric: This view exposes no aggregated metrics. All output columns are direct column projections (no aggregation).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to gene-dimension or gene-level normalized views on ensembl_gene_id — e.g., join to differential_expression_by_gene_disease on ensembl_gene_id — safe because this view is one row per (ensembl_gene_id, uniprotkb_ac) pair and differential_expression_by_gene_disease is one row per ensembl_gene_id and disease (ensure the DE view is aggregated to the same grain you expect). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to healthy_expression_by_gene_anatomy on ensembl_gene_id — safe when the target view is aggregated to one row per ensembl_gene_id (or when you expect a 1-to-many relationship from the expression view and handle it accordingly). | DO NOT join this view without care to a one-to-many table by ensembl_gene_id (for example, join to a table listing many transcripts, many variants, or many articles per gene) unless you either (a) aggregate the downstream one-to-many table first back to ensembl_gene_id, or (b) re-aggregate after the join. Doing an unguarded join to a one-to-many detail table will multiply rows for a given (ensembl_gene_id, uniprotkb_ac) and thus duplicate any measures derived from row counts. | Do NOT assume uniqueness of uniprotkb_ac per ensembl_gene_id: the LEFT JOIN to map_protein_disease_mutation can yield multiple uniprotkb_ac values for the same ensembl_gene_id (this view's grain explicitly includes uniprotkb_ac). If your downstream aggregation requires one row per ensembl_gene_id, you must choose an aggregation rule (e.g., ARRAY_AGG, MIN/MAX, take canonical) before joining. | Joining to map_uniprot_canonical_id on uniprotkb_ac is safe within this view because the join is performed with map_uniprot_canonical_id.uniprotkb_ac = map_protein_disease_mutation.uniprotkb_ac; if map_uniprot_canonical_id contains multiple canonical rows per uniprotkb_ac then duplicates could occur — treat map_uniprot_canonical_id as one-to-one only if enforced by data constraints. If not guaranteed, aggregate canonical mapping to one row per uniprotkb_ac before joining to avoid duplication. | When composing with sibling JOIN views that are protein-centric (for example, biomarker_with_aliases_and_articles or disease_mutation_with_annotations), prefer joining on uniprotkb_ac when you require protein-level joins. Understand that this view's grain includes ensembl_gene_id as well as uniprotkb_ac, so joining protein-centric views that are one-row-per-uniprotkb_ac is safe only if the mapping between ensembl_gene_id and uniprotkb_ac is one-to-one in your data or you've pre-aggregated to a single uniprotkb_ac per gene. | If you need a strict one-row-per-ensembl_gene_id result before further joins: aggregate this view by ensembl_gene_id (for example, choose a canonical uniprotkb_canonical_ac using MAX/MIN or ARRAY_AGG and pick the first element) and then join other tables — this prevents measure duplication.

gene_ensembl_to_uniprot_map.description: Mapping from gene_symbol/ensembl_gene_id to UniProt canonical accession where available by chaining xref_gene_ensembl -> map_protein_disease_mutation -> map_uniprot_canonical_id. One row per ensembl_gene_id + uniprotkb_ac mapping. Useful when linking gene-centric results to protein identifiers. | Use for: Map gene symbols/ensembl ids to UniProt accessions; Join proteomic data (Uniprot) back to gene- or transcript-level observations; Resolve canonical UniProt accession for downstream aggregation by protein

anatomical_entity_lookup.name: anatomical_entity_lookup
anatomical_entity_lookup.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  name,
  description
FROM anatomical_entity

params.description: Lookup of anatomical entities by id with canonical name and description.
params.when_to_use: Resolve an anatomical entity id to its human-readable name and description. | Annotate other result sets that reference anatomical entity ids (e.g., expression or biomarker records) with entity name/description. | Compose into queries that need a stable one-row-per-anatomical-entity dimension for joins or filters.
params.output_schema: id: unique identifier for the anatomical entity (directly from anatomical_entity.id) | name: canonical name of the anatomical entity (directly from anatomical_entity.name) | description: textual description or definition of the anatomical entity (directly from anatomical_entity.description)
params.metric: id = anatomical_entity.id | name = anatomical_entity.name | description = anatomical_entity.description
params.composition: Cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to this view on anatomical_entity.id (the view is one-row-per-id) — safe because anatomical_entity.id is the grain (one row per id) so joining this view to fact tables keyed by anatomical_entity.id will not duplicate this view's rows or measures. | Safe to join from fact/result tables that reference a single anatomical_entity.id per row (for example healthy_expression_by_gene_anatomy on its anatomy_id or equivalent) — the anatomical_entity_lookup simply supplies descriptive attributes and does not change cardinality. | Do NOT join this view to a one-to-many table/view that expands anatomical_entity.id into multiple rows (for example a hypothetical anatomy_aliases table with multiple aliases per id) without re-aggregation, because that would multiply rows when composed into metrics and could incorrectly duplicate counts or measures. If you must join to such a one-to-many source, aggregate the downstream measures back to anatomical_entity.id (e.g., SUM/COUNT/GROUP BY anatomical_entity.id) before combining with this lookup. | When composing with sibling normalized views (e.g., differential_expression_by_gene_disease, healthy_expression_by_gene_anatomy, disease_summary): join on the column that contains the anatomical entity id in the sibling view to anatomical_entity.id. This is safe because anatomical_entity_lookup is a dimension (one row per id) and these siblings are facts or normalized results; ensure the sibling view does not itself represent multiple rows per anatomical entity for the same measure if you expect a 1:1 correspondence.

anatomical_entity_lookup.description: Simple projection of anatomical entities (ontology id and descriptive fields). Useful as a stable dimension to join to expression, EDRN or mutation tissue mappings. | Use for: Show human-readable tissue names for uberon ids; Filter anatomical entities by name and join to expression or mutation tissue tables

disease_summary.name: disease_summary

params.description: Provides the canonical list of diseases (id and name) at one row per disease.
params.when_to_use: Look up disease metadata (id and human-readable name) for display or filtering. | Join disease identifiers to other datasets (e.g., expression, mutations, biomarkers) when you need one row per disease. | Compose higher-level aggregations by joining disease-level measures (e.g., counts per disease) onto this canonical disease dimension.
params.output_schema: id: disease identifier (derived from disease.id) | name: disease name / label (derived from disease.name)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to fact or many-sided views on disease.id — safe because disease_summary is one-row-per-disease (primary key = id), so joining disease_summary to a many-row fact by disease.id will not duplicate the disease_summary rows' meaning; e.g., join differential_expression_by_gene_disease on disease.id to enrich expression facts with disease name. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to sibling normalized dimension views (one-row-per-key) on id — safe because both sides are one-to-one on disease.id, e.g., if there were another disease-dimension view with the same grain. | do NOT join to one-to-many enrichment/detail tables/views (e.g., biomarker_with_aliases_and_articles, disease_mutation_with_annotations, biomarker_edrn_with_anatomy) expecting the resulting rows to remain one-per-disease without re-aggregation — those joins will multiply disease_summary rows because those sibling views contain multiple rows per disease.id. If you need disease-level measures after such joins, aggregate (GROUP BY disease.id, disease.name) or use COUNT(DISTINCT ...) as appropriate. | when composing metrics, preserve the disease_summary grain (id) as the join key and, if pulling measures from many-to-one facts, aggregate the fact first to disease.id to avoid accidental row multiplication.

disease_summary.description: Projection of disease table useful as a stable dimension for joins to mutation or FDA test disease identifiers (doid). | Use for: Lookup disease names for doid values; Join disease names to mutation or test records
validated_on: Return the symbol and p-value for the expression of EGFR in lung cancer
Show name of diseases where the gene expression with symbol A1BG has a statistical significance of 'Yes'
counter_examples: Show all information about diseases where the name contains 'cancer'
Show name of diseases where the A1BG gene expression is statistically significant
Get the biomarker gene symbol and biomarker description for disease with name 'breast cancer'

biomarker_edrn_with_anatomy.name: biomarker_edrn_with_anatomy
biomarker_edrn_with_anatomy.body_sql:
SELECT
  be.id,
  be.qa_state,
  be.biomarker_title,
  be.biomarker_type,
  be.uberon_anatomical_id,
  ae.name AS anatomical_name,
  be.phase
FROM biomarker_edrn be
LEFT JOIN anatomical_entity ae
  ON ae.id = be.uberon_anatomical_id

params.description: Provides one-row-per-biomarker records enriched with associated anatomical entity name (via uberon id); answers what biomarkers exist, their QA state, type, phase, and linked anatomy.
params.when_to_use: Look up biomarker metadata and associated anatomy for a given biomarker id or list of ids. | Filter or group biomarkers by anatomy (Uberon id or anatomical name), biomarker_type, phase, or qa_state. | Compose into downstream analyses that need biomarker-level attributes (e.g., joining to aliases, articles, tests, or expression results) while preserving one-row-per-biomarker granularity.
params.output_schema: id: unique biomarker identifier; derived from biomarker_edrn.id | qa_state: quality-assurance state of the biomarker record; derived from biomarker_edrn.qa_state | biomarker_title: human-readable title/name of the biomarker; derived from biomarker_edrn.biomarker_title | biomarker_type: categorical type of the biomarker (as stored); derived from biomarker_edrn.biomarker_type | uberon_anatomical_id: foreign key to anatomical_entity (Uberon ontology id) associated with the biomarker; derived from biomarker_edrn.uberon_anatomical_id | anatomical_name: readable anatomy name looked up from anatomical_entity.name; derived from anatomical_entity.name (aliased as anatomical_name) | phase: clinical/validation phase or phase-like attribute of the biomarker; derived from biomarker_edrn.phase
params.grounded_columns: biomarker_edrn.id | biomarker_edrn.qa_state | biomarker_edrn.biomarker_title | biomarker_edrn.biomarker_type | biomarker_edrn.uberon_anatomical_id | biomarker_edrn.phase | anatomical_entity.id | anatomical_entity.name
params.metric: This view exposes no aggregated metrics. All output columns are direct column projections (identity mappings) from base tables. | No derived numeric aggregates present; any counts/summaries must be computed by the caller.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to biomarker_with_aliases_and_articles on biomarker_with_aliases_and_articles.id = biomarker_edrn_with_anatomy.id — safe because this view is one-row-per-biomarker (grain = id) and the sibling view is expected to also be one-row-per-biomarker (or to supply distinct alias/article aggregations); verify the sibling's grain before joining if it is one-to-many. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to fda_test_rank_by_gene_count on biomarker id only if that view is one-row-per-biomarker; otherwise aggregate the one-to-many side first. The biomarker_edrn_with_anatomy view itself will not duplicate measures when joined to one-row-per-biomarker dimension views on id. | DO NOT directly join this view to one-to-many tables/views (for example: a raw articles table that contains multiple rows per biomarker, alias lists, or expression result tables) without either (a) aggregating the many-side to one row per biomarker first (e.g., GROUP BY id, produce counts/arrays), or (b) performing a DISTINCT/ROW_NUMBER window to reduce to one row per biomarker. Otherwise the biomarker-level rows (its logical measures) will be multiplied. | Safe join keys (one-to-one or many-to-one into this view): join on biomarker id (biomarker_edrn_with_anatomy.id) when the other side is a dimension keyed by biomarker id; join on uberon_anatomical_id to anatomical_entity or anatomical_entity_lookup if those are one-row-per-anatomy (this view already includes anatomical_name from anatomical_entity). | Examples of unsafe direct joins without re-aggregation: biomarker_with_aliases_and_articles if implemented as one row per alias/article (would multiply biomarker rows); expression result views (differential_expression_by_gene_disease, healthy_expression_by_gene_anatomy) which are typically many-per-gene or many-per-anatomy — aggregate or filter them to biomarker-level before joining. | When composing aggregates (counts, averages) over this view, compute aggregates after any joins to many-sided data, or pre-aggregate the many-side and then join on id to preserve correct cardinality.

biomarker_edrn_with_anatomy.description: EDRN biomarker records joined to anatomical entity names where uberon_anatomical_id matches anatomical_entity.id. One row per biomarker_edrn record; anatomy may be NULL if no match. Useful for filtering EDRN biomarkers by tissue or showing tissue names. | Use for: Find EDRN biomarkers associated with a particular anatomical entity; List EDRN biomarkers and their QA state or phase along with tissue names
validated_on: What are the different biomarker EDRN phases?

fda_test_rank_by_gene_count.name: fda_test_rank_by_gene_count
fda_test_rank_by_gene_count.body_sql:
SELECT
  test_trade_name,
  test_submission,
  biomarker_origin,
  doid,
  histological_type,
  specimen_type,
  platform_method,
  test_number_genes,
  test_adoption_evidence,
  test_approval_status,
  test_study_design,
  clinical_significance,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY doid ORDER BY COALESCE(test_number_genes, -1) DESC) AS test_number_genes_rank
FROM biomarker_fda_test

params.description: Ranks FDA biomarker tests by the number of genes per disease (DOID), returning test-level attributes and a rank per disease based on test_number_genes.
params.when_to_use: Find the top (or N) FDA tests for a given disease by number of genes covered | Compare test-level attributes (platform, specimen, approval status, evidence) for tests within the same disease | Compose downstream analyses that need one row per test_submission/test_trade_name with a disease-level ranking by gene count | Filter to tests above/below a gene-count threshold and retain disease-relative ordering
params.output_schema: test_trade_name: trade name of the FDA test, derived from biomarker_fda_test.test_trade_name | test_submission: unique submission identifier for the FDA test, derived from biomarker_fda_test.test_submission | biomarker_origin: origin/source of the biomarker/test, derived from biomarker_fda_test.biomarker_origin | doid: disease identifier (Disease Ontology ID) used as the partition key for ranking, derived from biomarker_fda_test.doid | histological_type: histological type associated with the test, derived from biomarker_fda_test.histological_type | specimen_type: specimen type required/used by the test, derived from biomarker_fda_test.specimen_type | platform_method: platform or method used by the test (e.g., NGS), derived from biomarker_fda_test.platform_method | test_number_genes: numeric count of genes covered by the test, derived from biomarker_fda_test.test_number_genes | test_adoption_evidence: evidence level for adoption of the test, derived from biomarker_fda_test.test_adoption_evidence | test_approval_status: approval status of the test (e.g., cleared/approved), derived from biomarker_fda_test.test_approval_status | test_study_design: study design associated with test validation, derived from biomarker_fda_test.test_study_design | clinical_significance: clinical significance annotation for the test, derived from biomarker_fda_test.clinical_significance | test_number_genes_rank: integer rank (1 = largest test_number_genes) computed per doid using ROW_NUMBER() over PARTITION BY doid ORDER BY COALESCE(test_number_genes, -1) DESC; derived expression, not stored in base table
params.grounded_columns: biomarker_fda_test.test_trade_name | biomarker_fda_test.test_submission | biomarker_fda_test.biomarker_origin | biomarker_fda_test.doid | biomarker_fda_test.histological_type | biomarker_fda_test.specimen_type | biomarker_fda_test.platform_method | biomarker_fda_test.test_number_genes | biomarker_fda_test.test_adoption_evidence | biomarker_fda_test.test_approval_status | biomarker_fda_test.test_study_design | biomarker_fda_test.clinical_significance
params.metric: test_number_genes_rank = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY doid ORDER BY COALESCE(test_number_genes, -1) DESC) | test_number_genes = biomarker_fda_test.test_number_genes (base numeric column; used as sort key for ranking)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE: join to disease_summary on doid (e.g., fda_view.doid = disease_summary.doid) — safe because this view is one-row-per test_submission/test_trade_name; joining to a disease dimension that is one-row-per-doid will not duplicate this view's rows or its measures. | cardinality-SAFE: join to anatomical_entity_lookup on specimen_type (e.g., fda_view.specimen_type = anatomical_entity_lookup.anatomical_entity_id) — safe when the lookup is one-row-per-anatomical-entity, it enriches rows without duplicating measures. | cardinality-SAFE: join to gene_ensembl_to_uniprot_map or disease_mutation_with_annotations only if you first aggregate those one-to-many sources to one row per test_submission or per doid (e.g., pre-aggregate gene-level rows into counts or lists keyed by test_submission or doid). If you pre-aggregate to test_submission, you can then join on test_submission safely because the view is one-row-per test_submission. | DO NOT join directly to biomarker_fda_tests_w_drugs_ncit or biomarker_with_aliases_and_articles (or any other one-to-many child tables keyed to test_submission or test_trade_name) without re-aggregation: those joins are one-to-many and will multiply this view's rows and thus duplicate or inflate measures like test_number_genes and the ranking context. Instead, either (a) aggregate the child table to one row per test_submission (e.g., COUNT(drug) AS n_drugs) and then join on test_submission, or (b) build compositions that re-calculate ranking/metrics after the join. | When joining to sibling views that are normalized per gene (e.g., differential_expression_by_gene_disease) or per anatomy (healthy_expression_by_gene_anatomy), do not join directly unless you aggregate the sibling view to the same grain (test_submission or doid) first. Direct joins to gene-level or many-to-many views will create multiplicative expansions and invalidate the per-doid ROW_NUMBER() ranking. | If you need to compute derived measures across joins (e.g., average test_number_genes by platform_method after joining to a platform dimension that is many-to-one), prefer aggregating test_number_genes in a grouped query on this view (GROUP BY platform_method) rather than joining and then summing child rows, to preserve correct counts.

fda_test_rank_by_gene_count.description: Ranking of biomarker_fda_test rows per doid by test_number_genes in descending order producing a rank column test_number_genes_rank. Useful as a reusable ranking CTE for Top-K tests per disease when combined with a downstream WHERE test_number_genes_rank <= K. | Use for: Select top-K FDA tests by number of genes for a disease (doid); Compare tests within a disease ranked by panel size

disease_mutation_rowlevel.name: disease_mutation_rowlevel
disease_mutation_rowlevel.body_sql:
SELECT
  dm.id AS id,
  dm.chromosome_id AS chromosome_id,
  dm.chromosome_pos AS chromosome_pos,
  dm.ref_nt AS ref_nt,
  dm.alt_nt AS alt_nt,
  dm.ensembl_transcript_id AS ensembl_transcript_id,
  dm.cds_pos AS cds_pos,
  dm.peptide_pos AS peptide_pos,
  dm.aa_pos_uniprotkb AS aa_pos_uniprotkb,
  dm.ref_aa AS ref_aa,
  dm.alt_aa AS alt_aa,
  dm.mutation_freq AS mutation_freq,
  dm.data_source AS data_source,
  dm.doid AS doid
FROM disease_mutation dm
disease_mutation_rowlevel.description: Row-level view exposing disease_mutation rows and all raw columns useful for filtering, projection, and joins. No aggregations; suitable as the base cohort for queries about specific amino-acid changes, genomic positions, transcripts, or disease (doid).

disease_mutation_with_tissue_and_article.name: disease_mutation_with_tissue_and_articles
disease_mutation_with_tissue_and_article.body_sql:
SELECT
  dm.id,
  dm.chromosome_id,
  dm.chromosome_pos,
  dm.ref_nt,
  dm.alt_nt,
  dm.ensembl_transcript_id,
  dm.cds_pos,
  dm.peptide_pos,
  dm.aa_pos_uniprotkb,
  dm.ref_aa,
  dm.alt_aa,
  dm.mutation_freq,
  dm.data_source,
  dm.doid,
  -- arrays lifted from literals: tissue uberon ids and article pmids
  COALESCE(array_agg(DISTINCT dmt.uberon_anatomical_id) FILTER (WHERE dmt.uberon_anatomical_id IS NOT NULL), ARRAY[]::character varying[]) AS tissue_uberon_ids,
  COALESCE(array_agg(DISTINCT dma.pmid) FILTER (WHERE dma.pmid IS NOT NULL), ARRAY[]::bigint[]) AS article_pmids
FROM
  disease_mutation dm
  LEFT JOIN disease_mutation_tissue dmt ON dmt.disease_mutation_id = dm.id
  LEFT JOIN disease_mutation_article dma ON dma.disease_mutation_id = dm.id
GROUP BY
  dm.id,
  dm.chromosome_id,
  dm.chromosome_pos,
  dm.ref_nt,
  dm.alt_nt,
  dm.ensembl_transcript_id,
  dm.cds_pos,
  dm.peptide_pos,
  dm.aa_pos_uniprotkb,
  dm.ref_aa,
  dm.alt_aa,
  dm.mutation_freq,
  dm.data_source,
  dm.doid
disease_mutation_with_tissue_and_article.description: Denormalized mutation-level view joining disease_mutation to supporting tables for tissue (uberon) and linked articles/annotations. One row per disease_mutation.id with arrays/lists of related pmids and tissue uberon ids (if present). Useful for questions that need mutation details plus context (tissue, literature).

disease_mutation_functional_predictions.name: disease_mutation_functional_predictions
disease_mutation_functional_predictions.body_sql:
SELECT
  dm.id,
  dm.chromosome_id,
  dm.chromosome_pos,
  dm.ref_nt,
  dm.alt_nt,
  dm.ensembl_transcript_id,
  dm.ref_aa,
  dm.alt_aa,
  dm.mutation_freq,
  dm.data_source,
  dm.doid,
  -- lift literal separators out of the view: use ',' as array_to_string separator when needed in downstream queries;
  -- here we produce aggregated arrays (nullable) so consumers can stringify as desired.
  array_agg(dmp.id ORDER BY dmp.id) FILTER (WHERE dmp.id IS NOT NULL) AS prediction_id_list,
  array_agg(dmp.tool ORDER BY dmp.id) FILTER (WHERE dmp.tool IS NOT NULL) AS prediction_tools_list,
  array_agg(dmp.probability ORDER BY dmp.id) FILTER (WHERE dmp.probability IS NOT NULL) AS prediction_probabilities_list,
  array_agg(dmp.site_prediction ORDER BY dmp.id) FILTER (WHERE dmp.site_prediction IS NOT NULL) AS prediction_site_predictions_list
FROM disease_mutation dm
LEFT JOIN disease_mutation_impact_prediction dmp
  ON dmp.disease_mutation_id = dm.id

biomarker_with_fda_tests.name: biomarker_with_fda_tests
biomarker_with_fda_tests.body_sql:
SELECT
  bfda.id                                                  AS "biomarker_fda.id",
  bft.test_trade_name                                       AS test_trade_name,
  bft.test_submission                                       AS test_submission,
  bft.biomarker_origin                                      AS biomarker_origin,
  bft.test_manufacturer                                     AS test_manufacturer,
  bft.test_approval_status                                  AS test_approval_status,
  bmk.biomarker_id                                          AS biomarker_id
FROM biomarker_fda                         bfda
-- join to linking table that associates biomarker_fda rows to biomarkers (if present)
LEFT JOIN biomarker_fda_ncit_term          bfda_n
  ON bfda.id = bfda_n.biomarker_fda_id
LEFT JOIN biomarker_fda_drug               bfda_d
  ON bfda.id = bfda_d.biomarker_fda_id
-- join to canonical FDA test records that keep one row per test_trade_name / test_submission
LEFT JOIN biomarker_fda_test               bft
  ON bfda.test_trade_name = bft.test_trade_name
  AND bfda.test_submission = bft.test_submission
-- try to associate a biomarker row via biomarker_fda.id -> biomarker_fda... tables to biomarker.biormarker_id
-- There is no direct FK to biomarker table in the schema; we attempt to join via biomarker_fda_drug or biomarker_fda_ncit_term
-- to biomarker.biomarker_id or biomarker.biomarker_id-like fields. Fallback: attempt join by matching biomarker_id to bfda.id as a best-effort.
LEFT JOIN biomarker                         bmk
  ON bmk.biomarker_id = bfda.id
-- If the schema links biomarkers to FDA entries through the biomarker_fda_drug or biomarker_fda_ncit_term
-- by a shared identifier, attempt to resolve via those alias/drug/ncit entries (this preserves biomarker internal id if present)
LEFT JOIN biomarker                         bmk_via_drug
  ON bfda_d.biomarker_drug = bmk.biomarker_id
LEFT JOIN biomarker                         bmk_via_ncit
  ON bfda_n.ncit_biomarker = bmk.biomarker_id
WHERE TRUE
biomarker_with_fda_tests.description: One row per FDA test record joined to the biomarker id where available (denormalized view linking biomarkers to FDA test entries via biomarker_fda -> biomarker_fda_test / biomarker_fda_test_use). Useful for queries that need biomarker attributes plus FDA test metadata. Keeps FDA test rows granular (one row per test_submission / test_trade_name combination).

differential_expression_direction_normal.name: differential_expression_direction_normalized
differential_expression_direction_normal.body_sql:
SELECT
  de.gene_symbol,
  de.doid,
  de.log2fc,
  de.pvalue,
  de.adjpvalue,
  de.expression_change_direction,
  -- canonicalize is_upregulated:
  -- treat 'up', 'increased', '+', or any value starting with 'up' or '+' (case-insensitive) as upregulated
  -- treat 'down', 'decreased', '-', or values starting with 'down' or '-' as not upregulated
  -- NULL or other values map to NULL
  CASE
    WHEN de.expression_change_direction IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN LOWER(de.expression_change_direction) LIKE 'up%' THEN true
    WHEN LOWER(de.expression_change_direction) = '+' THEN true
    WHEN LOWER(de.expression_change_direction) LIKE '+%' THEN true
    WHEN LOWER(de.expression_change_direction) LIKE 'increas%' THEN true
    WHEN LOWER(de.expression_change_direction) LIKE 'down%' THEN false
    WHEN LOWER(de.expression_change_direction) = '-' THEN false
    WHEN LOWER(de.expression_change_direction) LIKE '-%' THEN false
    WHEN LOWER(de.expression_change_direction) LIKE 'decreas%' THEN false
    ELSE NULL
  END AS is_upregulated,
  -- canonicalize statistical significance into boolean:
  -- treat common indicators ('significant', 'yes', 'true', 's', 'sig') or adjpvalue/pvalue thresholds if raw flag missing
  CASE
    WHEN de.statistical_significance IS NOT NULL THEN
      CASE
        WHEN LOWER(de.statistical_significance) IN ('significant','sig','s','yes','true','y','1') THEN true
        WHEN LOWER(de.statistical_significance) IN ('not significant','notsignificant','ns','no','false','n','0') THEN false
        ELSE NULL
      END
    WHEN de.adjpvalue IS NOT NULL THEN
      -- common threshold: adjpvalue < 0.05 => significant
      CASE WHEN de.adjpvalue < CAST('0.05' AS double precision) THEN true ELSE false END
    WHEN de.pvalue IS NOT NULL THEN
      CASE WHEN de.pvalue < CAST('0.05' AS double precision) THEN true ELSE false END
    ELSE NULL
  END AS is_statistically_significant,
  de.subjects_total
FROM differential_expression_by_gene_disease de
differential_expression_direction_normal.description: Normalized view that canonicalizes expression_change_direction and statistical_significance into machine-friendly flags (is_upregulated, is_stat_sig) while preserving raw values. One row per differential_expression (gene_symbol, doid).

SELECT

  COALESCE(ba.alias, NULL) AS alias,

FROM biomarker b
-- left join to biomarker_alias by biomarker internal id (alias may be NULL)
LEFT JOIN biomarker_alias ba_alias
  ON ba_alias.biomarker_internal_id = b.id
-- left join to biomarker_article by biomarker internal id (pmid may be NULL)
LEFT JOIN biomarker_article ba_article
  ON ba_article.biomarker_internal_id = b.id
-- combine alias and pmid rows: use a lateral union of the two sources per biomarker
-- but since view must be a single SELECT body without WITH, simulate by selecting from biomarker and unnesting array of pairs
-- Build arrays of aliases and pmids then unnest them in parallel to produce all combinations
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT
    a.alias AS alias,
    NULL::character varying AS pmid
  FROM biomarker_alias a
  WHERE a.biomarker_internal_id = b.id

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    NULL::character varying AS alias,
    p.pmid AS pmid
  FROM biomarker_article p
  WHERE p.biomarker_internal_id = b.id
) ba ON TRUE

biomarker_core_normalized.name: biomarker_core_normalized
biomarker_core_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- primary canonical id: prefer EDRN registry id if present, else biomarker.id
  COALESCE(bedrn.id, b.id) AS id,
  -- qa_state from EDRN if available, else NULL
  bedrn.qa_state AS qa_state,
  -- canonical title: prefer EDRN title, else biomarker_description, else biomarker_id
  COALESCE(bedrn.biomarker_title, b.biomarker_description, b.biomarker_id) AS biomarker_title,
  -- canonical type: prefer EDRN type, else biomarker.test_is_a_panel indicator mapped to 'panel'/'single' as fallback
  COALESCE(
    bedrn.biomarker_type,
    CASE
      WHEN b.test_is_a_panel IS TRUE THEN 'panel'
      WHEN b.test_is_a_panel IS FALSE THEN 'single'
      ELSE NULL
    END
  ) AS biomarker_type,
  -- anatomy: prefer EDRN uberon id, else NULL
  bedrn.uberon_anatomical_id AS uberon_anatomical_id,
  -- phase from EDRN if available
  bedrn.phase AS phase,
  -- internal biomarker id (carry through): prefer biomarker_internal_id from aliases/articles view, else biomarker.id
  COALESCE(bwa.biomarker_internal_id, b.id) AS biomarker_internal_id,
  -- gene symbol: prefer biomarker.gene_symbol, else NULL
  b.gene_symbol AS gene_symbol
FROM
  biomarker b
  -- left join to EDRN registry (one row per EDRN.id linking by some match: match on biomarker_id = edrn.id OR biomarker.id = edrn.id)
  LEFT JOIN biomarker_edrn bedrn
    ON (b.biomarker_id IS NOT NULL AND b.biomarker_id = bedrn.id)
    OR (b.id IS NOT NULL AND b.id = bedrn.id)
  -- join to provided view that brings internal ids/aliases and articles when available
  LEFT JOIN biomarker_with_aliases_and_articles bwa
    ON bwa.id = b.id
biomarker_core_normalized.description: Canonicalized biomarker records combining primary biomarker table and EDRN registry fields where available, normalizing NULLs and exposing standard id/gene/title/type/phase/anatomy columns for analysis and filtering.

biomarker_phase_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  -- canonicalize phase: trim whitespace, collapse internal whitespace, lower-case for normalization,
  -- but preserve NULLs. Lifted literal: '' (empty string) treated as NULL.
  CASE
    WHEN phase IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN regexp_replace(btrim(phase), '\s+', ' ', 'g') = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE lower(regexp_replace(btrim(phase), '\s+', ' ', 'g'))
  END AS phase_normalized,
